title: Structure of the programming message according to the syntax graphic
body_md: The graphic shows a continuous character string and assigns four explanations to it by means of lines: the country code beginning with a plus sign, a leading marker for the case where the end device is a smartphone, and the destination numbers in their order, the first of which is the master number. The graphic explains the smartphone marker as switching the position transmission to a clickable link and limits its use to smartphones.
source_region: Section 2.8, syntax graphic in the lower third of the page
prev_context: Before this stands the introduction to section 2.8.
next_context: The example table and section 2.9 follow on the next page.
change_reason: Extracted from the English source page itself, not translated from the German master, and cross-read against the German page 16: the same graphic with identical example values and identical assignment lines; only the labels are translated and the example country differs (DSC-019). The example values are not reproduced (BLK-006). Important layout finding: in the German part this graphic occupies an internal page of its own, whereas the English version places it together with the introduction to 2.8 – the cause of the page displacement recorded in DSC-021.
